title: W5' fix defect: plate press-swallow kills the two rightmost tray chips (visible but unclickable while D is on)
evidence: app/main.odin:1201 `if app.overlay_on && rnd.noc_panel_hit(rnd.noc_panel_rect(app.view.win_w, app.view.win_h), pos) {` (+1202 `return true`) — runs before the input layer's tray loop (app/input/mouse.odin:304 `if ui {` / :311 `} else {` tray loop :319 `if rl.CheckCollisionPointRec(left_press, rnd.tray_chip_rect(inp.view, i)) {`). app/render/tray.odin:48 `x0 := (f32(v.win_w) - total_w) / 2` — 6 chips (3 tiers + 3 junctions) x 96 + 8 gap = 616px -> tray spans x 332..948 at 1280; noc_panel_rect.x = 1280-524 = 756, so chips 4 (router_mid, 748..844) and 5 (router_high, 852..948) sit over the plate, which draw_tray paints OVER (draw_hud after the rail). The PR body's claim 'the clickable surfaces — QoS, tray, chip, popover — are all inside the playfield' is false for the win_w-centered tray.
detail: The bottom band floats over the plate by design (Perkins r1 W1), so the tray's rightmost chips are drawn over the plate yet their presses are swallowed before the tray loop — router_high can never be armed with D on at the design resolution.
recommended_fix: Exempt the floating bottom band from the swallow: skip the plate return-true when pos hits a tray chip rect (tray_chip_rect loop) so those presses fall through to the input layer's tray hit-test, or re-center the tray on play_w while the rail is on.

title: noc_panel_rect's 'single source' comment is inaccurate — the draw path re-derives the plate inline
evidence: noc_overlay.odin:364 `// The hit-test + the draw share it (single source — the tests pin the rect).` vs the actual draw at noc_overlay.odin:630-631 `rl.DrawRectangle(px - NOC_PLATE_PAD, 0, NOC_RAIL_W, v.win_h, NOC_PLATE)` / `rl.DrawRectangleLines(px - NOC_PLATE_PAD, 0, NOC_RAIL_W, v.win_h, NOC_PLATE_EDGE)` where `px := noc_panel_x(v.win_w)` (line 626). The draw never calls noc_panel_rect; the two derivations agree only because NOC_RAIL_W == NOC_PANEL_W + NOC_PLATE_PAD + NOC_PANEL_MARGIN.
detail: Two independent plate-geometry derivations (rect proc vs px-minus-pad inline) drift if the constant relation changes; the comment claims a sharing that does not exist in the project's canon-comment style.
recommended_fix: Have draw_noc_panel call noc_panel_rect(v.win_w, v.win_h) for the plate rect (deriving px as rect.x + NOC_PLATE_PAD), or drop the 'single source' claim from the comment.

title: Duplicated DOCK-RIGHT comment block in overlay_check
evidence: Lines 72-73 `// DOCK-RIGHT (fit-to-rail): the capture renders the app's D-on playfield` / `// (play_w = win_w - NOC_RAIL_W) so the frame matches the real run.` then again lines 76-79 `// DOCK-RIGHT (fit-to-rail): the capture renders the app's D-on playfield` / `// (play_w = win_w - NOC_RAIL_W) so the frame matches the real run — and` / `// view_refit re-derives scale/off from play_w (Perkins r1 W4: the world` / `// must fit LEFT of the rail, not extend under it).`
detail: Copy-paste leftover: the same two-sentence rationale appears twice back-to-back around the feed scan; noise in a file whose comments are treated as canon.
recommended_fix: Delete the first (shorter) instance at lines 72-73 and keep the fuller 76-79 block above view_set_rail.

title: View.play_w comment claims 'the harness never does' flip the rail — the harness overlay verbs do
evidence: view.odin:43-44 `// app flips it via view_set_rail (effect_overlay + boot/resize); the` / `// harness never does — T2 goldens are untouched by construction.` — contradicted by harness/overlay.odin:80 `rnd.view_set_rail(&rc.view, true)` (and the same call added in harness/font_check.odin this round). The T2-golden conclusion holds (the golden capture path never invokes the PP_DEBUG verbs), but 'the harness never does' is literally false.
detail: The field comment overstates the invariant: PP_DEBUG harness verbs now set the rail deliberately; a reader could wrongly conclude harness code must never touch view_set_rail.
recommended_fix: Reword to 'the harness T2 capture path never does (only the PP_DEBUG overlay verbs set it deliberately) — T2 goldens are untouched by construction.'
